provenance.citation: Shortliffe, E. H., & Buchanan, B. G. (1975). A model of inexact reasoning in medicine. Mathematical Biosciences, 23(3–4), 351–379. Reprinted as Chapter 11 in: Buchanan, B. G., & Shortliffe, E. H. (Eds.), Rule-Based Expert Systems. Addison-Wesley, 1984.
provenance.locus: Section 11.2 "MYCIN's Rule-Based Approach" (p. 238) — the illustrative rule used throughout the chapter; Section 11.4 (p. 247) — MB[h,e] = 0.7 derivation for the same rule.
provenance.notes: The 1975 paper presents exactly one fully worked rule: gram-positive + coccus + chains → streptococcus with CF 0.7 (Section 11.2, p.238). The rule numbering RULE050/RULE071 does NOT appear in this paper — those labels come from the full MYCIN dissertation (Shortliffe 1976). The paper uses this single rule throughout as its running example to derive the MB/MD/CF formalism. The therapy step (penicillin) is mentioned only in the chapter abstract and broader MYCIN context; the CF 0.9 for the therapy rule is from secondary sources (Shortliffe 1976). The existing fixture's three-premise streptococcus rule and two-step chain are consistent with the paper but the paper specifies exactly three premises: (1) gram-positive stain, (2) coccus morphology, (3) grows in chains — the existing fixture omits the 'chains' premise, which is the third condition stated verbatim on p.238.

input.intent: diagnose bacteremia organism and recommend antibiotic therapy

expected.notes: Paper states MB[h,e]=0.7 for the streptococcus rule (p.247). The expert gave '7 out of 10' certainty (p.238 fn4). Corrected this session: therapy_cf is the CHAINED certainty (0.9 rule certainty * 0.7 organism_cf = 0.63) per the accumulation formula this note itself describes, not the therapy rule's own raw certainty (0.9) -- confirmed against production_rules.rs's own passing unit test (shortliffe_1975_organism_cf_07_therapy_cf_063). Combined CF via accumulation formula: CF_final = CF_old + CF_new*(1-CF_old) is the update law described in the full MYCIN system.
